pages.title: Right to die with dignity — Harish Rana case

facts.text: Supreme Court allowed withdrawal of life support for Harish Rana — right to die with dignity part of Article 21
facts.head: News

facts.text: Rana injured in a fall in 2013 (aged 20); in Persistent Vegetative State (PVS) for 13+ years, on CANH
facts.head: News

facts.text: Held: CANH (Clinically Assisted Nutrition and Hydration) is medical treatment; withdrawal in patient's best interest (family + medical boards)
facts.head: News

facts.text: Case: Gian Kaur v. State of Punjab (1996); Holding: Right to live with dignity; ⚠ rejected right to die
facts.head: Evolution of law

facts.text: Case: Aruna Shanbaug v. Union of India (2011); Holding: Passive euthanasia allowed in exceptional cases
facts.head: Evolution of law

facts.text: Case: Common Cause v. Union of India (2018); Holding: Right to refuse treatment; living wills; guidelines simplified in 2023
facts.head: Evolution of law

facts.text: Passive euthanasia: withholding/withdrawing life-sustaining treatment — legal under strict conditions
facts.head: Evolution of law

facts.text: Article 21 cases: Hussainara Khatoon (speedy trial); Suchita Srivastava, Puttaswamy (reproductive choice)
facts.head: Evolution of law

facts.text: ⚠ First time the SC actually implemented passive euthanasia in a specific case; active euthanasia remains illegal
facts.head: More facts

facts.text: P. Rathinam (1994) had recognised a right to die under Article 21 — overruled by Gian Kaur (1996); 2023 simplified living wills
facts.head: More facts
